rules.statement: Replace hardcoded magic numbers and literal strings in logic with named constants or configuration options.
rules.why: The maintainer counts unexplained hardcoded values as 'duct tape' technical debt that makes code fragile and hard to understand.
rules.check: Look for unexplained numeric or string literals in conditionals, timeouts, sizes or limits that are not named constants or bound options.

rules.statement: Use the project's existing abstraction for a concern instead of bypassing it with direct calls to the underlying implementation.
rules.why: Bypassing established abstractions adds coupling and inconsistency, which builds up technical debt across incremental patches.
rules.check: Look for new code that reaches past an existing service, interface or helper (for example, it calls a lower-level API directly when the project already wraps it).

rules.statement: Do not add special-case conditionals or workarounds that patch a symptom; fix the underlying logic or design instead.
rules.why: The maintainer's main concern is complex conditionals that look like temporary fixes and pile up as patch upon patch.
rules.check: Look for new if or switch branches keyed on specific values, flags or edge cases that exist only to work around a bug somewhere else.

rules.statement: Move logic that is repeated in the change into a shared reusable method or component instead of duplicating it.
rules.why: The review asks for repeated logic to be refactored, following the DRY principle, so the code stays maintainable.
rules.check: Look for blocks of code in the diff that are the same or nearly the same, or that copy logic already in the codebase.

rules.statement: Handle every failure path explicitly, including null inputs, timeouts and failed external or API calls.
rules.why: The maintainer requires production-ready code that covers all failure paths instead of relying on fragile assumptions.
rules.check: Look for external calls with no timeout or cancellation and no error handling, and for inputs dereferenced without null or validity checks.

rules.statement: Validate input and enforce authentication and authorization checks on every API endpoint.
rules.why: The review treats missing auth checks or input validation as a security risk in the API contract.
rules.check: Look for new or changed endpoints or handlers that accept request data without validating it, or that have no authorization requirement.

rules.statement: Do not hardcode secrets or credentials in source code or committed configuration; load them from a secure configuration source.
rules.why: The review requires environment variables and secrets to be handled securely.
rules.check: Look for passwords, keys, connection strings with credentials, or tokens written as literals in code or appsettings files.

rules.statement: Avoid N+1 query patterns: do not issue a database query per item inside a loop when one batched query can fetch the data.
rules.why: The review asks whether queries are optimized and calls out N+1 problems explicitly.
rules.check: Look for database or repository calls inside loops over a result set, and for lazy-loaded navigation access inside iterations.

rules.statement: Run multi-step data modifications that must succeed or fail together inside a single transaction.
rules.why: The review requires transaction integrity and data integrity to be kept.
rules.check: Look for several related writes or SaveChanges calls in one operation with no surrounding transaction.
